pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to Embley School | Private school in Romsey, Hampshire
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Embley School | Private school in Romsey, Hampshire
Children progress from Embley as Renaissance individuals, formed into intellectually curious and open-minded young people who seek their personal best in all that they do and are adept at being effective navigators in a sea of change. They are successful, rounded, happy and compassionate young people who don’t think less of themselves, just think of themselves less.
Latest from Embley
VIEW ALL NEW STORIES
Academic exploration in Cambridge
Mastering hill skills in Dartmoor
Eric Twiname Racing Championships
Layton Williams @ Embley
By allowing children to be purposefully uncomfortable, they embrace experiences that provide opportunity to see the world from different perspectives.
Compassion at Embley
Embley Commended for Outstanding Fundraising
Embley has been commended in the Independent School of the Year Awards for Outstanding Fundraising Achievement!
Tradition
It has been a week of very interesting conversations. One such was a conversation I had with a young couple and we talked about their aspirations for their children and, in particular, what makes a good school.
To be authentically human is to engage our capacity to reason. Children develop a keen analytical awareness and an ability to discern effectively.
Enquirers at Embley
Sailing for Silver!
A group of Year 10 students recently completed their Silver Duke of Edinburgh expedition sailing with the Morning Star Trust.
With liberty
In an act of fairly unsurprising (given the time) injustice to its co-author, John Stuart Mill’s essay On Liberty was originally published without listing his wife’s contribution. This was only corrected decades later.
“Our role is to create a generation of young people who will make the world a better place. We shape children to focus on being ‘their’ best. They arrive at a destination that may seem ‘the best’ but are not complacent to settle there. An Embley education brings out a level of achievement in the children that they didn’t know they had.”
As an innovative and forward-looking school, we are purposefully suited to the challenges of the modern world. Our focus is on the formation of young people who don’t just believe in success, they live it authentically.
Beyond their own A*
Our focus is on the formation of authentic and successful young people who can become anything they want to be.
We take children beyond what statistics say they can do. Your child will leave Embley with a promising future ahead of them, a portfolio of strong academic results, a finely tuned emotional and intellectual toolkit.
Embley is an HMC accredited school.
We are a Prep, Senior School and Sixth Form as one; on one breath-taking site and with one shared vision for our children. From the early years of childhood to the final days of Sixth Form, this is a journey we are on together; each member of staff with each child in our care.
A 130 acre classroom
Learning at Embley is not contained by public exam specifications. Alongside a rich academic curriculum sits our programme of over 200 co-curricular experiences, each specifically designed to develop life-long skills that enhance learning and personal development. Set amidst a stunning 130- acre woodland campus, we believe that academic progression and personal wellbeing are enhanced by outdoor adventure, serving others, playing sport and participating in the Arts.
Adventure & Service
From learning about duty and service at our partner school in Ghana, community projects closer to home, our Combined Cadet Force and Duke of Edinburgh programme, to understanding the importance of teamwork and building resilience while sailing on Embley’s fleet of keelboats and trekking the three highest peaks in Scotland, there is nothing better
than seeing the delight on children’s faces when they are allowed to be purposefully uncomfortable and realise what they are capable of.
Explore Adventure & Service
Sport at Embley
We don’t chase silverware, we chase performance because we believe it is the challenge to improve, the resolve to endure and the drive to succeed that inspires the journey rather than the destination. Our focus is on how we get better,
incrementally, humbly recognising how we improve and master our craft. The ‘prize’ is improvement, the silverware just acknowledges it.
The Arts
From being immersed in one of our artist in residence workshops in our purpose-built art studios, to taking to the stage in a whole school Broadway productions to a sell-out audience, or playing alongside acclaimed pianists and composers, we instil a love, appreciation and respect for the
Arts. Embley is alive with the Arts and there’s no better way to experience this than at our annual, rival to Edinburgh, Embley Fringe.
We are Embley
"The overall purpose of Embley is ‘the formation of children’ and clearly education is a part of that. But here, they teach scientists and not students of science – it’s contextualised, meaningful, collaborative, analytical and creative - an intoxicating blend formulated to cultivate inquisitive and thoughtful young people."
“We found the children to be wholesome and curious, with few inhibitions. When we asked them what they liked about the school, one threw her arms in the air and roared 'everything!'"
Read the Good Schools Guide review of our Senior School
"A dynamic, forward-thinking school in a stunning location, where pupils are encouraged to 'find what makes them tick' (whatever that may be) and stretched and challenged to 'be their best selves'."
Read the Good Schools Guide review of our Prep
“Being part of this school has been such a wonderful experience. This is the best decision we’ve made for our children."
“There are so many opportunities at Embley to challenge myself. A sense of adventure is actively encouraged, and I've developed the confidence to step outside my comfort zone and to be more curious which has really helped me with my studies and to understand more about me as an individual.”
“Parents unwavering in their praise for the school's 'focus on the individual', the opportunities beyond the classroom and the 'incredible teachers' who 'nurture their confidence'.”

pageCache.text:
The Embley Experience | About Us | Embley, private school in Hampshire
The Embley Experience
Committed to being our best
Embley is more than an education. We are a school purposefully suited to the opportunities of the modern world – our aim is the deliberate and purposeful ‘formation’ of young people. Our children go out into the world as capable, independent, interested and interesting individuals.
The highest levels of achievement are regularly and impressively met at Embley, but they are the result of progress. Progress is achievement. We are a community committed to getting better; where the value of making mistakes is understood, and no one flies under the radar.
We want children to be challenged, stretched, excited and listened to; to be purposefully uncomfortable, and able and willing to stretch themselves. Our focus is on children achieving their best; being the best may elude them or not, it is of no consequence. Effort and attitude at Embley is always focused on being our best, the rest will follow.
A School for the Renaissance Child
Embley is a proudly innovative school, but with heritage. From deep and important roots that reach as far back as the Domesday Book, we look forward.
We are a modern independent school standing tall on the shoulders of our heritage where the path of our future is one of progress. Ours is a school for the Renaissance child; for the curious, the enquirers, for those with a passion to learn and a capacity for wonder.
There is no ‘type’ here. We are not a factory bent on producing the same product time after time. Our girls and boys are surrounded by a huge range of opportunities to discover – academic and artistic, personal and professional. It is not our purpose to produce more accountants, medics, and lawyers; our mission is to form authentic young people confident in themselves who can become any of those things and more.
Led by inspirational teachers
Great teachers are the heartbeat of Embley. No grandeur of place or sophistication of facility can replace meaningful relationships in a classroom where our teachers spark interest and intrigue.
The way a teacher inspires you, believes in you, or just makes you love to learn is truly invaluable. Embley attracts, keeps, and develops those people.
We have a constant desire for improvement, our aim is to ‘be better’; to use the latest teaching and learning research and resources. We have all the rigour, all the achievement, but none of the unnecessary pressure without merit that blights childhoods. Some pressure is a necessary part of life – it is healthy, it drives us on – but it must be used with consideration. We will know every child’s progress to the smallest detail without ever letting it loom over them.

Learning | Nursery & Pre-School | Embley, private school in Hampshire
NURSERY & PRE-SCHOOL
Learning
Nursery
From the age of two, children blossom in a nurturing and caring environment. As well as literacy and numeracy, each week your child will benefit from dedicated Music, PE and Natural Science lessons with our specialist Prep teachers.
They will start to develop letter and sound recognition in phonics and number recognition in maths, along with their listening and attention skills, understanding of the world, arts and crafts and expressive arts. With a carefully crafted combination of child- and adult-led activities, learning is tailored to a child’s interests and the next stages of their development.
Pre-School
As your child moves into our Pre-School, they are introduced to a more structured environment but still with lots of opportunities for play and discovery centred around their interests.
They will start each day with maths and phonics lessons, working in small groups and learning to work as a team. French is introduced into the curriculum alongside our specialist teaching for Music, PE and Natural Sciences. We help children develop their listening and concentration skills, which includes mindfulness activities such as yoga, threading and dough disco. In the Summer term, the children enjoy a number of transition sessions where they explore the Reception classroom with their new teacher. Our children are led by our Head of Early Years, who is a qualified teacher and all our Nursery & Pre-School staff are qualified Level 3 Early Years practitioners as a minimum.
Early Years Curriculum
Our carefully crafted Early Years curriculum centres around areas for school readiness:
Listening attentively, following instruction, expressing themselves and being aware of others around them.

Job vacancies and careers | Embley School, independent education in Romsey, Hampshire
Careers at Embley
Embley is a wonderful and inspiring place to work. We are proud to be one of the most innovative, ambitious and forward-thinking independent schools in the UK.
By combining the passion and expertise of our teachers and business support staff with forward-thinking teaching and learning practices, exceptional facilities, and the latest technologies, we unlock the potential in every child and help them grow.
We have nearly 200 staff working at Embley across a range of teaching and operational departments, with a strong emphasis on continuing personal development. Training is delivered at Inset days and twilight sessions across the academic year with a programme covering the latest developments in teaching, sharing of best practice and insights from visiting educational experts, including Winchester and Southampton universities and TES.
Staff work collaboratively and observe each other regularly, with professional conversations to support development. This not only ensures our continuous focus on high quality teaching and learning but reinforces our mutually supportive professional relationships at Embley. Subject specific training is also encouraged to ensure staff have the latest knowledge of their curricula and specifications.
All teachers receive free membership to the Chartered College of Teaching and a subscription to the College’s peer-reviewed journal and networking opportunities. As part of the United Learning group, we also offer access to PGCE and QTS training. Click here to find out more.
Vacancies
Thank you for your interest in working at Embley. There are currently no vacancies.
Benefits of working at Embley
A comprehensive employee benefits package supports wellbeing, work-life balance and long-term financial security.
Excellent support and training for trainee teachers
Contributory pension scheme
Health cash plan with Westfield Health
Life insurance and free will-writing service
250+ discounts through Westfield Rewards
Free school lunches during term time
Car lease salary sacrifice scheme
Discounted gym membership
RAC discounts
Local area and transport links to Embley
Located in the heart of the English countryside and on the edge of the New Forest, Embley is within easy reach of cities including Winchester, Southampton and Salisbury.
Southampton Central and Southampton Parkway have fast train connections to London. From Romsey, there is a direct line to the West country passing through Salisbury, Bath and Bristol to Cardiff, and Southampton and Portsmouth to the East. Embley is easily accessible by road, being five minutes from the M27 at Junction 2.

Nursery & Pre-School | Embley School, a private school in Romsey, Hampshire
NURSERY & PRE-SCHOOL
Welcome to our Nursery & Pre-School
Providing the perfect environment for a lifetime of learning to begin.
Behind a joyful atmosphere and hive of activity, you will find a meticulous approach to the formation of every child.
Each morning sees children running through our doors without a backwards glance.
Children join us from the age of 2 and follow a progressive development path as part of the Early Years curriculum that prepares them for the passage from toddler to school age.
With Embley Prep just next door to our self-contained Early Years Department, the transition could not feel more natural to both parent and child when the time comes.
Meet Emblington the Explorer
Meet Emblington the Eagle Owl, who is taking his first big step on his journey to become an explorer. To do so, he will experience new adventures at Embley Nursery & Pre-School alongside his new friends and learn that school is a doorway to magic and wonder.
A journey together
In a purposeful, fun and supportive environment, we travel on a journey together; each member of staff with each child in our care.
Every aspect of Nursery and Pre-School life is carefully crafted to help your child grow.
Our staff’s exuberance for every child’s development shines through the variety of inspiring activities enjoyed each day as we capture imaginations and make meaning through learning.
Learning
Your child will become an active explorer as they discover more about the world around them and start developing lifelong skills for learning. We introduce academic subjects in a way that fosters a child’s natural sense of curiosity and wonder, independence, collaboration and creativity. Every day includes activities to support mathematics, literacy and scientific discovery.
French, Music and PE are led by our specialist Prep teachers and in Natural Science lessons - which has cross curricular links with our Prep Science and Geography curriculum - the children learn in our outdoor classroom in the woods.
Adventure
Whatever the weather, we always have fun adventures exploring the outdoors. Surrounded by our 130 acres of parkland and woodland, there is plenty of space for your child to spread their wings and develop a love of nature.
We also venture on trips to enhance our curriculum such as to the beach, to learn about the ocean and coastal environment, and our monthly visits to the local public library, to support communication and language development.
Nursery &
Pre-School Day
Underpinning your child’s learning is a team of highly experienced teachers who plan meticulously but also work spontaneously to ensure every child’s curiosity is captured, making lessons fun and purposeful each day.
Your child can start the day with breakfast as early as 08:00 and finish after a light supper at 18:00. All our meals, including lunch, are freshly prepared and made by our resident chef using healthy ingredients.
Preparing for Prep School
There is a real focus at Embley to create a happy, safe and secure environment for our children, where they can feel confident developing their independence. We recognise that, as a parent, it is a big step to put your trust in others to look after the wellbeing and development of your child.
We make sure that the start of school is a fun time and we help with any nerves which may arise. By the time your child starts their new learning adventure at Prep, they will already feel part of our whole school community.
We are Embley
A message from our Head of Early Years
“Embley Nursery & Pre-School is a truly magical place where we create a learning environment that enhances every child’s exploration of the world, focused around what interests and excites them as a result.
"We tap into their awe and wonder through magical learning experiences as part of a dynamic and engaging curriculum, and we love seeing their learning skills, confidence and independence grow as a result."
ROSIE HIGH, HEAD OF EARLY YEARS

Geography trip to Morocco
Students from Year 8 and 9 had an incredible experience exploring Morocco on a week-long geography tour.
Abseil for Alzheimer's
Our Embley community showed off their courage, compassion and community spirit in an unforgettable challenge.
Turtle Conservation in Greece
Years 10 to 13 students have been taking part in hands-on turtle conservation activities in Kefalonia.

Adventure | Nursery & Pre-School | Embley, independent education in Hampshire
NURSERY & PRE-SCHOOL
Adventure
Wellies are part of the way of life and your child will spend plenty of time exploring and learning outside in our beautiful countryside location.Whatever the weather, our children have huge adventures exploring the school’s grounds with our 130 acres of parkland and woods offering plenty of room to spread their wings and develop a love for nature as they grow vegetables, enjoy treasure hunts, go on minibeast safaris and climb trees. Bushcraft skills such as sawing, fire lighting, den building, hammering and peeling are developed in our wonderful outdoor classroom in the woods.
Nursery & Pre-School Trips
We believe that children should experience the world beyond environments that they are used to as part of their learning and development.Your child will join us as we venture on trips to enhance our curriculum, such as to the beach close by, or monthly visits to the local public library to support communication and language development. We welcome special visitors into our Nursery & Pre-School to run workshops with the children and enjoy themed days (which often involve dressing up!) throughout the year.

NURSERY AND PRE-SCHOOL
Nursery and Pre-School Day
Days start at 08:30 and finish at 15:30, but to help busy parents we also offer a breakfast club for children who want to arrive at 08:00 and an afterschool club and/or creche up to 18:00.
Lunch is homemade each day by our resident chef using local, fresh and healthy ingredients and we join the rest of the Prep School for lunch to help prepare for the move up to Reception class. We also provide a range of healthy snacks during the day and serve milk and water with snacks and at mealtimes.
We work with parents to ensure our children follow a consistent daytime sleeping pattern and there are sleeping bags to ensure that children are safe and comfortable in our quiet areas. We are also led by parents to ensure we provide a consistent approach to toilet training and we have lower toilets which are designed to encourage confidence and self-sufficiency.

pageCache.text:
The Arts at Prep School | Embley School, independent education in Romsey, Hampshire
The Arts
Our creative curriculum is an integral part of every child’s learning experience as they develop fundamental skills of expression, confidence, collaboration and self-discipline. Art, Drama and Music also form part of our co-curriculum, with inspiration often coming from our collabroations with Embley Senior School and Sixth Form students.
Art
Your child will learn about Art from an artist’s perspective in our purpose-built art studio, which is always a hub of activity.
Exploring the use of mixed media, schemes of work include making clay tiles in the style of William Morris, studying perspective to create Lowry-style paintings and exploring pop art and onomatopoeic explosions to create comic book style paintings in the style of Roy Lichtenstein. The children get hands-on in our workshop with Design & Technology tools as they design and complete their design projects, ranging from creating matchstick pyramids to understand structure and height or constructing battery-powered mini kit cars. Beyond the classroom, we offer a whole host of creative co-curricular activities including pottery, arts and crafts, chocolate making, embroidery and creativity club.
Drama
Drama at Embley immerses children into more experiential learning, with improvisations in class around themed topics and texts which complement our English curriculum.
Working with our Director of Drama and specialist Drama teachers, the children have the opportunity to take part in productions such as Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat and Aladdin, our annual Summer Year 6 production and a range of drama workshops with visiting artists. Our co-curricular activities include drama clubs, ballet and dance.
Music
Learning music brings a whole host of important benefits including coordination, pattern recognition, memory skills, confidence and perseverance.
Children from Nursery age have a dedicated music lesson each week, taught by one of our music teachers. Our special relationship with Romsey Abbey is an integral part of school life, with children participating in choral workshops with the Abbey’s Director of Music and performances in the Abbey.
Half of our Prep children elect to learn an instrument with one of our many expert peripatetic music tutors, including wind, string and brass instruments, as well as electric and acoustic guitar, drums, piano and singing. They also enjoy our many music groups including school choirs, orchestra along with recorder, guitar and ukulele group and perform at our Prep Recitals. Children are regularly entered for Associated Board of Music, Trinity and Rock School exams.
Arts Award
Our Embley Arts Award offers a broad range of opportunities and benefits to our children.
This pupil-led award helps children to establish and grow skills in the performing arts (with a choice of completing the award via Art, Music, or Drama). But in addition to completing a performance, they can build a much broader range of essential skills, including organisation, leadership, planning and teaching.
The Arts Award runs at different grade levels, so your child can progress through the programme during their time at Embley.

University & Career Prep Sixth Form | Embley School, private education in Romsey, Hampshire
University & Career Preparation
The world is changing, the workplace is evolving and different breeds of professionals and professionalism emerging. We assist students with their short-term goals and long-term aspirations as they explore what is possible and the steps to achieving their vision.
To deepen understanding of the professional world that could await them, students hear from industry and university speakers, degree apprenticeship providers and successful business people, from start-ups to multinational firms.
Our Careers Advisor and a dedicated careers resource ensures they make well informed decisions as well as provide support for identifying work experience opportunities, UK and international university choices and applications, as well as everything else that life after Embley holds.
Entry to university has become increasingly competitive in recent years. Our students are guided through every stage of the application process, giving them a competitive advantage by showcasing them at their best – through their academic ambitions, skills and career aspirations. Interview preparation includes an interview practice afternoon for all sixth formers with professionals from a range of professions and industries, and we draw on our teacher’s expertise for subject-specific interview practice ahead of university academic interviews.
Leaver destinations
Reflecting their individual aims and ambitions, our students go on to read a wide range of subjects including Chemical Engineering, Medicine, Veterinary Medicine, English, Music and Sound Recording, Computer Science, Business and Modern Foreign Languages, Law, Biochemistry and History.
A significant number of Embley leavers go on to study at Russell Group universities. An increasing number of students are securing highly competitive degree apprenticeships with Pfizer, IBM and JP Morgan to name a few, or choosing to study at universities across the world.

Prep School Academic Life | Embley School, private education in Romsey, Hampshire
Academic
Prep and Senior School teachers work closely together to deliver our whole school curriculum, with our teacher-led enquiry approach to learning, as part of the Embley Thinking Curriculum, providing a continuous thread that builds with the children as they move through the school.Children of all ages often come together for shared learning experiences including our whole-school weeks celebrating areas such as literature, poetry and wellbeing.
Up to Year 2, lessons are mainly taught by primary years specialists with subject specialists, who often work across our Prep and Senior Schools, teaching French, Music and Sport. As your child progresses through Prep, they will be increasingly taught by specialist teachers across all subjects, utilising our Science Lab, DT Workshop, Art Studio and Computer Science Hub. Children learn French from Nursery and Spanish from Year 5.
We have a strong reading culture and appreciation of books, with two inspiring libraries for the children.
English is driven by engaging texts and children write in a range of styles. Drama lessons are often inter-linked to our English curriculum, helping children to become confident in front of audiences; be it a school production, assembly or public speaking competition. Our popular Book Club, Film Club and the Embley Eagle Newspaper Club enable children to pursue their interests in creative writing outside of the curriculum.
Maths at Embley is as much about depth of thought and problem solving as it is developing the foundations of knowledge. By building confidence to tackle new challenges, children learn the thinking skills to apply their knowledge in unfamiliar situations. Learning is extended beyond the curriculum through our Maths Club, which sees Senior School students mentoring the younger years, and our Minecraft Education Club where problem solving and systems thinking is developed through play.
We place great emphasis on both the practical and theoretical in Science, with Marine Biology taught in Year 6 which includes regular fieldtrips on our keelboats in the Solent to source specimens to study in the classroom.
Our Natural Science curriculum has cross curricular links with Science and Geography. We investigate meteorology, astronomy and sustainability and make the most of our extensive grounds. We conduct environmental surveys and use scientific skills to create new habitats, homes and food for the invertebrate and bird species observed.
Through these lessons, your child will gain a greater understanding and appreciation of how the world works and the part we can all play in caring for it. Our ‘Wild Ones’ club sees children learning new skills in our classroom in the woods and STEM and Construction Club sees our pioneering young engineers at work.
Humanities cross into many aspects of our curriculum to allow for a greater understanding of our world.
In Geography, the children learn about primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary industries, how they generate jobs, influence global trade and are influenced by government policy. Geography and Science combine through real world important issues with a focus on biodiversity, distribution of natural resources, climate change and living sustainably, linking to the United Nations 17 Sustainable Development Goals.
In History, we look at the past, how this has influenced our present and may impact our futures by learning in sequence. For example, Year 6 learn about power, empire and democracy, starting with the growth and decline of the British Empire before moving onto migration and life as a migrant, the civil rights movement and how these periods of time compare to how we live today. Children approach challenging, historically-valued questions by learning to think, read and study like a historian, learning about change, cause, similarity and significance of the world which has lived before them. And from Year 1 to 6, Religious Studies are divided into the topic areas of faith, theology, and religion and world views.

Prep School Sport Programmes | Embley School, private education in Hampshire
Sport
We engage and inspire children across all ages and abilities so that every child will build their confidence through a range of sporting experiences.
In Years 1 and 2, we focus on building the foundations of physical literacy. Lessons centre around mastering core skills such as basic movement, balance, agility and coordination. During these years, children begin to explore Embley’s core sports.
From Year 3, children join our Games programme and play modified competitive games as they continue to develop physically, building their flexibility, strength and stamina. As children move up the school, opportunities to represent Embley in fixtures and tournaments increase.
Core sports
Our core competitive sports are rugby (boys), hockey (girls and boys), netball (girls) and cricket (girls and boys), with a squad training and fixture programme from Year 3. The children also take part in outdoor and adventurous activity challenges as part of our sports programme, including sailing, climbing and skiing. Additional recreational sports available include golf, athletics, tennis, ballet, cross country, swimming and gymnastics.
We are fortunate to have all our sports facilities onsite for all the children to enjoy. They include rugby pitches, an all-weather Astroturf pitch, athletics track, cricket nets, netball courts, a 9-hole course, a covered swimming pool and tennis courts.

Pre-Senior Baccalaureate | Embley, private school in Hampshire
Pre-Senior Baccalaureate
2040: The decade many of our children will start their careers, in a world unlikely to be defined by a single profession or linear career path but instead shaped by constant change and an increasing emphasis on uniquely human skills.
Pre-Senior Baccalaureate (PSB) at Embley
In a world evolving at an unprecedented pace, we believe true success will mean far more than academic achievement alone.
Young people need the confidence to lead, the curiosity to explore, the resilience to embrace change and the compassion to make a positive impact on others. They must learn to communicate with conviction, collaborate effectively and think independently. These qualities sit at the heart of our learning experience and underpin everything we do.
The PSB is an innovative framework of study designed to prepare children for the challenges of life as young adults, academically, personally and culturally. It reflects our vision of equipping children not only to navigate their futures but to help shape them. Through the Embley Pupil Profile and the PSB framework, we combine rigorous academic learning wtih the essential human skills that artificial intelligence and automation cannot replace.
The core skills of PSB
Embedded across our curriculum, co-curricular programme, educational visits and leadership opportunities, the PSB at Embley develops six essential competencies that support both academic and personal achievement.
Collaboration
Communication
Independence
Leadership
Thinking & Learning
Review & Improvement
More than academic success
Research consistently shows that resilience, confidence, motivation and self-awareness are strong indicators of long-term success. At Embley, our approach combines rigorous academic learning with opportunities that help children discover who they are and what they can achieve.
Whether performing on stage, competing in sport, exploring the outdoors, leading a school initiative or participating in community projects, every experience contributes to their development as capable, well-rounded young people.
The PSB provides a framework for recognising and celebrating that growth while helping children become more reflective, engaged and ambitious learners.
Discover Embley Prep
Visit our Prep School, meet our teachers and explore how an Embley education enables children to develop the knowledge, skills and confidence to thrive in the 21st century. To arrange a visit, please click here.

Embley awarded prestigious HMC accreditation | Latest News | Embley School, Hampshire
Embley awarded HMC accreditation
Embley is delighted to announce that it has been awarded the prestigious HMC (The Head’s Conference) accreditation, reinforcing the school’s position as one of the leading independent schools for girls and boys in the South of England.This recognition follows a rigorous application process, during which the school’s excellence in academic achievement and focus on individual development, along with the pupils’ authenticity and humility, were highly commended. Becoming part of HMC places Embley among the top 300 independent schools worldwide, underlining its commitment to academic excellence and the holistic development of every child. HMC is a globally respected professional association of Heads, synonymous with quality, innovation, and excellence in education. Pupils at HMC schools consistently achieve outstanding results, both academically and beyond the classroom. At the core of every HMC school is a dedication to a well-rounded education—one that combines academic ambition with exceptional pastoral care and co-curricular opportunities. Cliff Canning, Headmaster of Embley, a full member of The HMC, commented: “We are incredibly proud to receive HMC accreditation and join this prestigious group of leading independent schools. This achievement is a testament to the dedication of our entire school community and reflects Embley’s remarkable journey of growth and transformation. It reaffirms our unwavering commitment to providing the best education for our children, empowering them to become exceptional young people who will go on to make a difference in the world.” As a member of HMC, Embley will benefit from a wide range of training and continuous professional development opportunities for staff and it will become part of a network that promotes the discussion of national and international education issues and informs policy and public opinion with regards to the independent school sector.

pageCache.pageTitle: History of Embley | About us | Embley, private school in Hampshire
pageCache.text:
History of Embley | About us | Embley, private school in Hampshire
History of Embley
Embley first opened its doors as a school in 1946 but there is evidence of a settlement on the school’s site for over a thousand years. Embley features in the Domesday Book and is Anglo Saxon for 'clearing in the woods'.
The main building you see today was constructed in the late Tutor and Elizabethan period, with extensive additions in the years that followed. In 1825, Embley’s most famous residents, the Nightingale family, took possession of the estate. During their time at Embley, extensive alterations were made.
By the end of 1949, the Chapel (now the Embley Library), was moved to its current position, and completed in 1953. The Chapel’s organ was originally the property of the Blackwood Murray Family, built by hand by John Blackwood Murray at the age of 16. One of its parts, the Clarabella Stop, was originally in an organ that was washed ashore from a wrecked ship off the Spanish Armada in 1588.
Inside the Manor House
The original red brick house built around 1622 featured two large halls with a fine oak staircase between them leading up to the first-floor rooms, which still exists today as you enter the Manor House, although much extended since.
You can see this staircase when entering the house through the front door on the left-hand side where it dominates the reception area. The array of stags’ heads above is a reminder that the estate was considered to be one of the finest in the land for country sporting pursuits.
Off the hallway to the right is what used to be a billiard room (now the Nightingale Room) followed by the Drawing Room (now used as a meeting space and known as the Old Library) where many an evening of music and entertaining were held.
To the left of the hallway was the dining room with its vaulted domed ceiling. This room now serves as the main school library. Down the hallway from the main entrance is what was William Nightingale’s library (now the Headmaster’s Drawing Room). The most notable feature of this room is the hidden door. This was covered and painted in the same style as the shelves either side of it, so as to conceal its true nature.
Close inspection reveals Mr Nightingale’s impish sense of humour, for the titles there include Leather on Woods, Tales of the Doorway, Oaths Not Binding and Optical Delusions. The hidden door leads into what was then known as the Garden Room, described by Florence in 1839 as “one of the prettiest in the house, both as to paper and to everything.” It is now the Headmaster’s Study.
Gardens and grounds
The 1825 sale particulars record that 1,300 acres were planted, criss-crossed by many miles of gravel drives.
A grotto and a pyramidical fountain also existed but have since been removed. The Nightingales introduced the Wild Gardens, with their Long and Short Walks, and stocked them with species which are still rare.
At the top of the Long Walk stands the semi-circular stone seat popularly known today as ‘Cromwell’s Seat’ – so called because it was reputedly brought here by the Heathcotes from Hursley. Richard Cromwell, son of Lord Protector Oliver, was a former owner of Hursley Park.
The last private occupant was Mr Joseph John Crosfield, a garden designer, horticulturist and philanthropist. Mr Crosfield also made alterations to the property, one such alteration being the addition of the clock tower, rumoured to have been placed there so that he could see the time from the Walled Garden (now our Sports Hall), where he grew rhododendrons, peaches and apparently, principally, tomatoes! The clock continues to chime on the hour today.
Tradition has it that Florence Nightingale was seated beneath one of the giant cedars of Lebanon near the Manor House when she received the first of her callings from God on 7 February 1837.

Leadership & Governance | About Us | Embley, independent school in Hampshire
Leadership & Governance
An exceptional school requires leadership that is constantly in pursuit of progress and excellence.
Senior Leadership Team
Our Senior Leadership Team is responsible for the effective day to day running of the school. Each member of the team has specific responsibilities within the overall management of the school:
Governance of United Learning schools
Embley is part of United Church Schools Trust (UCST) (a United Learning charity). UCST is the proprietor of Embley and its trustees hold the ultimate legal responsibility for the governance of its schools. The Chair of UCST is Dr Rosalind Given-Wilson. Further information about the governance of United Learning’s schools, including its Trustees and the scheme of delegation, can be found on the United Learning website.
All United Learning schools have a local governing body (LGB); the Chair is appointed by the United Learning Group Board. Details of the Chair and members of Embley's local governing body can be found below, together with any financial or business interests.
Click here to view the Scheme of Delegation, which details which responsibilities are delegated by the Board to the Executive, Head Teachers and the LGB.
Local Governing Body
Our Local Governing Body acts as our critical friend and trusted advisor to the Senior Leadership Team. Members draw on their significant experience in finance and law, education, commerce and media, and benefit from the guidance of its Chair.
Governors meet four times each academic year to review Embley’s strategic plans, consider everyday life at the school, and discuss other pressing matters as they arise. Members of the Leadership Team often join these meetings to update on key areas of the school’s development. Our governors are:
The clerk to the Governing Body is Mrs Claire Brighton. Please direct any correspondence for the Local Governing Body to clerk@embley.org.uk
